hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext:
[swarmlord plugin] Multi-agent routing policy — Claude orchestrates; CLI agents execute.

You can delegate to many CLI coding agents (Codex, Kiro, Copilot, Gemini, OpenCode, Command Code, Muse Code, Antigravity, Aider, Goose, local LLMs) through ONE entry point:
  swarmlord-delegate [--agent <name>] --task-type <frontend|backend|tests|refactor|docs|research|review> --dir <repo-root> "<task>"
With no --agent, config/routing.json picks the first healthy agent for the task type (fallbacks cover missing / unauthenticated / quota-exhausted agents). Routing is the user's to edit — never treat the defaults as facts about which agent is "best".

WHEN to delegate: large, well-scoped, test-covered units — scaffolding, exhaustive tests, migrations, refactors, bulk reads that return a digest. WHEN NOT to: small, self-contained, or judgement-heavy tasks. Delegating a tiny task is a net loss (spec + round-trip + verification exceeds doing it yourself). The break-even judgment is yours, every time.

ISOLATION: every run works in its own git worktree on branch swarmlord/<task>-<agent>. Only you merge. Review the diff; never merge an agent branch sight unseen.

VERIFY (non-negotiable): an agent's self-reported success is a claim, not evidence. Check the SWARMLORD_RUN line (class, tests, files_changed), review the worktree diff, and run the tests yourself. A run that changed no files on a write task is a failure, not a pass.

HANDOFF: a whole test-covered task can move between agents (swarmlord-handoff): the receiving agent gets a capsule of the previous agent's runs, file changes, test results, and errors. Prefer handoff over re-delegating from scratch.

CIRCUIT BREAKER: every run is ledgered (.git/swarmlord/ledger.jsonl). If a file returns to a previous hash, the same error repeats twice, one agent reverts another, or the per-task budget is exceeded, the wrapper pauses the task, checkpoint-commits, writes a conflict report, and exits 16. Do NOT retry a tripped task — surface the report and ask the user.

PERMISSIONS: adapters run with narrow grants by default. Full-trust flags (--full-trust) are opt-in per run and unsafe outside a disposable container — never pass them casually.

Headless (claude -p): delegate synchronously; background jobs are for interactive sessions only. Full detail is in the `swarmlord` skill. Turn this notice off via the plugin's `coding_policy` option.
